extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to The Mathematical Intelligencer (Springer Nature journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, ethically declaring, and submitting manuscripts (articles, reviews, commentaries, creative pieces, figures, and supplementary material) to The Mathematical Intelligencer, including post-acceptance steps and policies on data, authorship, and conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal follows a single-blind reviewing procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peer review process for special/guest-edited issues is the same. If a guest editor authors an article in their issue/collection, they will not handle the peer review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies: that the work described has not been published before; that it is not under consideration for publication anywhere else; that its publication has been approved by all co-authors and responsible authorities at the institute where the work has been carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent or secondary publication may be justifiable in certain cases (e.g., translations) but must meet conditions; salami-slicing/publishing is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to include figures, tables, or text passages that have already been published elsewhere are required to obtain permission from the copyright owner(s) for both the print and online format and to include evidence that such permission has been granted when submitting their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material received without such evidence will be assumed to originate from the authors. Be aware some publishers do not grant electronic rights for free and Springer will not refund permission costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory online submission via SNAPP
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission to The Mathematical Intelligencer is handled electronically through Springer Nature’s SNAPP platform; authors must submit exclusively through SNAPP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click the 'Submit manuscript' button and upload all manuscript files following on-screen instructions. Provide declarations via the submission interface (e.g., Author Contribution, Competing Interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide all editable source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Please ensure you provide all relevant editable source files at every submission and revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to submit a complete set of editable source files will result in your article not being considered for review. For manuscript text submit in common formats such as .docx or LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX template and submission of compiled PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: For LaTeX submissions we encourage authors to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template when preparing a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the original source (including all style files and figures) and a PDF version of the compiled output. Do not use subfolders for LaTeX submission (e.g., for figures or bibliographic files).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations should be defined at first mention and used consistently thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes can be used to give additional information (may include citation of a reference in the reference list) but should not consist solely of a reference citation and should never include bibliographic details of a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to the text are numbered consecutively; footnotes to tables indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance values). Footnotes to title or authors are not given reference symbols. Always use footnotes instead of endnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgments of people, grants, funds, etc. should be placed in a separate section on the title page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The names of funding organizations should be written in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables are to be numbered using Arabic numerals and should always be cited in text in consecutive numerical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply a table caption explaining the components of the table. Identify previously published material by giving the original source as a reference at the end of the table caption. Footnotes to tables use superscript lower-case letters or asterisks and appear beneath the table body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic figure submission and file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all figures electronically and indicate what graphics program was used to create the artwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For vector graphics preferred format is EPS; for halftones use TIFF. MS Office files are acceptable. Name figure files with 'Fig' and the figure number, e.g., Fig1.eps. Vector graphics containing fonts must have fonts embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line art requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Line art is black and white graphic with no shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use faint lines/lettering; ensure legibility at final size. All lines should be at least 0.1 mm (0.3 pt) wide. Scanned line drawings and bitmap line drawings should have minimum resolution 1200 dpi. Vector graphics containing fonts must have fonts embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone (photograph) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Halftones are photographs, drawings, or paintings with fine shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If magnification is used indicate with scale bars. Halftones should have minimum resolution 300 dpi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination artwork resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination art (halftone + line art, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combination artwork should have minimum resolution 600 dpi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color art requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Color art is free of charge for print and online publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color illustrations should be submitted as RGB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure lettering and font guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: To add lettering use Helvetica or Arial (sans serif fonts). Keep lettering consistently sized throughout final-sized artwork, usually about 2–3 mm (8–12 pt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variance of type size within an illustration should be minimal. Avoid effects such as shading, outline letters, etc. Do not include titles or captions within illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and parts
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures are to be numbered using Arabic numerals and should be cited in text in consecutive numerical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure parts should be denoted by lowercase letters (a, b, c, etc.). If an appendix appears in your article and it contains figures, continue the consecutive numbering of the main text (do not use A1, A2, etc.). Figures in online appendices (Supplementary Information) should, however, be numbered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure captions format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure should have a concise caption describing accurately what the figure depicts; include captions in the text file of the manuscript, not in the figure file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure captions begin with the term 'Fig.' in bold type, followed by the figure number in bold. No punctuation should follow the number, nor end the caption. Identify all elements found in the figure in the caption; use boxes/circles as coordinate points in graphs. Identify previously published material by giving the original source as a reference at end of caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure placement and sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be submitted within the body of the text; size figures to fit in the column width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only if file size causes upload problems submit large figures separately. For large-sized journals figures should be 84 mm (double-column) or 174 mm (single-column) wide and not higher than 234 mm. For small-sized journals figures should be 119 mm wide and not higher than 195 mm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To give people of all abilities and disabilities access to the content of your figures, authors should ensure accessibility features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures should have descriptive captions (for text-to-speech); use patterns instead of or in addition to colors (for color-blind users); any figure lettering should have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI images policy (figures and SI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must check Springer’s policy on generative AI images and make sure their work adheres to the principles described therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy applies both to figures and supplementary information (SI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information (SI) accepted formats and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer accepts electronic multimedia files and other supplementary files to be published online along with an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply all supplementary material in standard file formats. Include in each file the article title, journal name, author names, affiliation and e-mail address of the corresponding author. Keep file sizes reasonable to accommodate downloads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary multimedia technical specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical requirements for audio, video, and animations submitted as supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspect ratio: 16:9 or 4:3. Maximum file size: 2 GB. Minimum video duration: 1 sec. Supported file formats include avi, wmv, mp4, mov, m2p, mp2, mpg, mpeg, flv, mxf, mts, m4v, 3gp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary text, presentations, spreadsheets, specialized formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for non-multimedia supplementary files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text and presentations: submit in PDF (not .doc or .ppt). Spreadsheets: .csv or .xlsx. Specialized formats such as .pdb, .wrl, .nb, and .tex can also be supplied. Multiple files may be collected in a .zip or .gz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary numbering, captions, and in-text citation
rubrics_metrics.description: If supplying any supplementary material, the text must make specific mention of the material as a citation, similar to figures and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to supplementary files as 'Online Resource' (e.g., 'Online Resource 3'). Name files consecutively, e.g., 'ESM_3.mpg', 'ESM_4.pdf'. For each supplementary material supply a concise caption describing the content. SI will be published as received without conversion, editing, or reformatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility requirements for supplementary files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript must contain descriptive caption for each supplementary material. Video files should not contain anything that flashes more than three times per second to avoid seizure risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should refrain from misrepresenting research results and follow rules of good scientific practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit to more than one journal simultaneously. Work should be original unless it's an expansion of previous work with transparency on re-use. Avoid salami-slicing. Present results clearly and honestly; no fabrication, falsification or inappropriate data manipulation (including image manipulation). Adhere to discipline-specific rules for acquiring/selecting/processing data. Journal may use software to screen for plagiarism. Authors should ensure permissions for software/questionnaires/scales used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation practices and self-citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and non-research articles must cite appropriate and relevant literature to support claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive and inappropriate self-citation or coordinated self-citation among authors is strongly discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid defamatory or untrue statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should avoid untrue statements about an entity or descriptions that could be personal attacks or allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-use / potentially harmful research notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that may be misapplied to pose a threat to public health or national security should be clearly identified in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include creating harmful biological agents, disrupting vaccine immunity, unusual chemical hazards, or weaponization of research/technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of data and supporting documentation upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request authors should be prepared to send relevant documentation or data to verify validity of results (raw data, samples, records, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitive confidential or proprietary data is excluded. Authors should ensure data transparency and that data/materials/code support published claims and comply with field standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct investigation and possible outcomes (per COPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is suspicion of misbehavior or alleged fraud the Journal/Publisher will carry out an investigation following COPE guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible outcomes: rejection if under consideration; if published, erratum/correction, expression of concern, or retraction depending on severity. Retraction remains on platform watermarked 'retracted' with explanation. The author’s institution may be informed. A notice of suspected transgression in peer review may be included in bibliographic record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of fundamental errors after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have an obligation to correct mistakes once they discover a significant error or inaccuracy in their published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should contact the journal and explain how the error impacts the article. Decision on correction or retraction depends on nature of error. Retraction note should provide transparency on parts impacted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting or excluding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are welcome to suggest suitable reviewers and/or request exclusion of certain individuals when submitting manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested reviewers must be totally independent and not connected to the work. Recommend a mix from different countries and institutions. Corresponding Author must provide an institutional email for each suggested reviewer or other means to verify identity (personal homepage, publication record, researcher ID). The Journal may not use suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure (authors and editorial members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are requested to disclose interests directly or indirectly related to the submitted work; Editorial Board Members and Editors must declare any competing interests and may be excluded from handling manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report interests within the last 3 years of beginning the work; interests outside 3 years must be disclosed if they could reasonably be perceived as influencing the work. Types include funding, employment, financial interests (stocks, consultancies, patents), and non-financial interests (positions, consulting, mentoring). Primary research and review articles require a disclosure statement; other article types may require depending on content. Funding information must be disclosed in submission interface and summarized in 'Declarations'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations section and sample wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of requirements should be placed in a 'Declarations' section before the reference list under headings like 'Funding' and/or 'Competing interests'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of wording are provided for funded work, no funding, and items to declare. When all authors have the same/no conflicts a blanket statement suffices. Authors are responsible for correctness; Editor-in-Chief reserves right to reject submissions not meeting guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data policy and Data Availability Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal follows Springer Nature research data policy; sharing relevant research data is strongly encouraged and authors must add a Data Availability Statement to original research articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data availability statements should explain how to access data supporting the results, including links/citations to archived datasets. If data cannot be shared (e.g., privacy), describe how data can be accessed and conditions for reuse. Participant consent should be obtained and documented. Consider the minimal dataset necessary to interpret/replicate findings. Guidance, examples, and links to repositories and mandated data types are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data repositories, citation, and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to deposit supporting data in publicly available repositories and to cite publicly available data used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discipline-specific repositories where available; certain data types may mandate specific repositories. Encourage open licences that permit reuse. Data citations should include a persistent identifier (e.g., DOI) and follow DataCite minimum information in the reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymisation when sharing data during double-anonymous review
rubrics_metrics.description: If providing reviewers with access to data in a double-anonymous peer review context, it is suggested that authorship in the data is also anonymised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data repositories can assist or create masked links to hide authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship principles and recommended criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Publisher recommends authors adhere to authorship guidelines (e.g., ICMJE): listed authors should have made substantial contributions; drafted or revised critically; approved the version to be published; and agree to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher does not prescribe exact contribution types; in absence of field-specific rules authors should follow the recommended criteria. Include disclosures and declarations as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding Author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: One author is assigned as Corresponding Author and acts on behalf of all co-authors and ensures questions about accuracy/integrity are addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include ensuring all listed authors approved the manuscript and author order, managing communication between journal and co-authors (may be delegated), providing transparency on re-use of material, and making sure disclosures, declarations and data statements from all authors are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contributions statements and CRediT taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: In fields where possible, authors are recommended to include contribution statements specifying the contribution of every author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: free-text statements or CRediT taxonomy roles (Conceptualization, Methodology, Formal analysis, Writing - original draft, Writing - review and editing, Funding acquisition, Resources, Supervision, etc.). For review articles include who had the idea, who did literature search/data analysis, who drafted or critically revised. For dissertation-based articles recommend student as principal author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliations and author name accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary affiliation for each author should be the institution where the majority of their work was done; current addresses may additionally be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses will not be updated after publication. Ensure names are present and correctly spelled; names will be published exactly as they appear on the accepted submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding/deleting authors, changes in corresponding author, or changes in author sequence are not accepted after acceptance of a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding/deleting authors at revision stage are generally not permitted but may be warranted with explanation; approval of change during revision is at Editor-in-Chief discretion. Reasons for changes must be explained. Authorship disputes during peer review or after publication should be resolved by authors; if unresolved the Journal may withdraw the manuscript or raise issue with authors' institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author identification (ORCID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to use their ORCID ID when submitting an article or acquire an ORCID via the submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased or incapacitated authors guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a co-author dies or is incapacitated during writing, submission, or peer-review and co-authors wish to include them, co-authors should obtain approval from a legal representative (e.g., direct relative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of journal communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should treat all communication with the Journal as confidential, including correspondence with Editors-in-Chief, Handling Editors and reviewers’ reports unless explicit consent to share has been received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance production and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance the article is exported to Production for typesetting; authors will receive emails to confirm affiliation, choose publishing model, arrange rights/payment, and a link to proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of proof is to check typesetting/conversion errors and completeness/accuracy of text, tables and figures. Substantial changes in content (new results, corrected values, title/authorship) are not allowed without Editor approval. After online publication further changes only via Erratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article publishing agreement and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on journal ownership/policies you will either grant the Publisher an exclusive licence to publish or be asked to transfer copyright to the Publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Choice articles do not require transfer of copyright; authors agree to publish under a Creative Commons license when opting for open access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Choice (open access) option
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Choice allows publication open access in many Springer Nature journals; APCs vary by journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include increased visibility, higher access and citations, and easier compliance with funder mandates. Open Choice articles keep copyright with the author and are published under CC licences; see journal's 'How to publish with us' guide for licence details and funding/support pages for APC funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of editing services
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent editing services (Springer Nature Author Services) can help with manuscript preparation (English editing, developmental comments, formatting, figure preparation, translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using these services is not a requirement and does not imply or guarantee acceptance or selection for peer review. Free Grammar Check tool is available.
